newsitem.title: USA: Teen arrested in U.S. abortion clinic attacks.
newsitem.headline: Teen arrested in U.S. abortion clinic attacks.

text.p: A 15-year-old boy was arrested on Thursday and charged with carrying out three bomb and gunfire attacks at an abortion clinic in Tulsa, Oklahoma, U.S. officials said.

Federal agents arrested the teenager at a suburban home on Thursday morning after getting a tipoff from someone who saw a composite sketch of the main police suspect in the attacks, all of which occurred in the first five weeks of this year.
Justice Department officials said the boy was taken before a U.S. magistrate and charged on five counts of using explosive devices and firearms in violent crime and possessing a firearm.
Unconfirmed local television reports said FBI agents had found explosives at the boy's home in the Tulsa suburb of Bixby.
FBI spokesman Dan Vogel said a man, a woman and an eight-year-old child were placed in custody and questioned, but that they were later released. "We are only making one arrest today."
The boy's name was not released because he is a juvenile and Vogel declined to detail what evidence had been found at the home.

The Reproductive Services Clinic in Tulsa has been attacked three times since the start of 1997. On New Year's Day, two molotov cocktails were thrown at the building and two small bombs were exploded outside the back door on January 19.
Last Sunday, someone broke into the building and fired bullets into medical equipment.
No one was injured in the attacks as the clinic was closed on all three occasions. The clinic employs 15 people and offers family planning and adoption services as well as abortions.
Vogel said the investigation was continuing and more arrests might be made.
